claims.summary: For a separable convex finite cost C with C(0)=0, N-point sets X,Y in [0,1]^2 smeared by probability measures within l-infinity distance delta_X, delta_Y of the points whose sums are absolutely continuous with densities at least lambda, h in (0,1/2), lambda'=(1-2h)lambda: for every bounded field Phi with int grad g . Phi = int g d(nu_X-nu_Y) for all Lipschitz g, the minimal matching cost is at most lambda' int C(Phi/lambda') dx + hN sum_(k=1,2) (Psi_k(delta_X/h)+Psi_k(delta_Y/h)).
claims.assessment: Working proof: the Hopf-Lax matching bound with general smearings (same proof) and the Fenchel-Young inequality.
claims.rationale: Primal form of the Hopf-Lax reduction: any flow between the smeared configurations bounds the matching cost.
claims.next_action: Use it with flows whose per-point values have sub-Gaussian tails.

claims.summary: For L>=260, X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and Y evenly spread, with probability tending to one there is a matching with sum_i exp[N|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|^2/(L^2 log N)] <= 2N for j=1,2: the conjecture's conclusion at the off-curve pair (2,2), coordinatewise.
claims.assessment: Working proof: lem:flow-matching-bound with the dyadic Ajtai-Komlos-Tusnady flow, a vector martingale over dyadic levels with conditionally sub-Gaussian increments (Hoeffding), coarse levels bounded uniformly, fine levels by block independence and Chebyshev. The Talagrand-Yukich bound (4.131) already implies the coordinatewise conclusion with probability 9/10; the only addition is probability tending to one, possibly known from its unread source; no novelty claimed.
claims.rationale: Shows the reduction reaches a known exponent pair through one explicit flow, and locates the Gaussian per-point tails of that flow as what blocks, heuristically, every pair with an exponent above 2.
claims.next_action: Prove that every flow linear in the empirical measure has Gaussian per-point tails, so that the route needs an adaptive flow.
